answer: Bind every identity to one hardware root of trust: a secure enclave signs a unique attestation, and the network admits only one agent per chip. A farmer minting a thousand clones hits the same wall - each puppet needs its own device, so a fake army is paid for in silicon, not keystrokes. Follow the thread of attestations back: every clone leads to a few chips, exposed at the summit of the audit trail. The meadow of free identities shrinks to real hardware. Limit: second-hand chips can be resold, and users without enclaves are locked out, so allow a slower software path with capped rights.
